$description: Semantic stacking-order contract for Mission Platform. Categories are separated by the shared scale and leaves within a category use 50-point steps so media, application surfaces, overlays, features, and diagnostics layer predictably.

z-index.$description: Use these named layers instead of numeric z-index literals. Lower categories render behind higher categories; adjacent leaves within a category are separated by 50 points.

base.$description: Foundational layers inside an isolated component, including media backgrounds and local foreground controls.

media.$description: Media backgrounds sit behind the component's normal content.

media-overlay.$description: Media scrims sit above media and below the component content.

content.$description: Normal component content provides the base application surface.

foreground.$description: Local controls and raised content sit above the base component surface.

navigation.$description: Persistent navigation and local navigation menus that sit above ordinary page content.

navbar.$description: Sticky or fixed navigation bars remain above page content.

menu.$description: Navigation menus and submenus sit above their navigation bar.

floating.$description: Transient anchored surfaces that float above navigation and ordinary content.

dropdown.$description: Dropdowns, select menus, and autocomplete lists use this floating layer.

popover.$description: Anchored popovers render above dropdown menus.

tooltip.$description: Tooltips and truncation hints render above other anchored surfaces.

overlay.$description: Application overlays and their content surfaces that cover or interrupt the page.

backdrop.$description: Overlay backdrops dim the page behind an overlay surface.

panel.$description: Overlay panels, command palettes, and related transient surfaces sit above their backdrop.

drawer.$description: Dismissible side and edge drawers, with the scrim below the drawer panel.

backdrop.$description: Drawer backdrops cover the page immediately below the drawer panel.

panel.$description: Drawer panels render above their backdrop and page content.

modal.$description: Modal and guided-education surfaces that require the user's attention.

dialog.$description: Dialog and modal surfaces render above drawers and application overlays.

onboarding.$description: Onboarding tour layers render above modal dialog surfaces.

notification.$description: Persistent or transient notifications that remain visible above application surfaces.

toast.$description: Toast containers remain above modal and onboarding surfaces when announced.

cookie.$description: Cookie-consent banners and settings surfaces remain above ordinary notifications.

feature.$description: Feature-specific internal layers that must remain above their component surfaces but below diagnostics.

table.$description: Sticky table headers and loading surfaces sit above table content.

editor.$description: Rich-text editor selection and block controls sit above editor content.

planner.$description: Resource-planner sticky headers and resource columns preserve their grid layering.

scheduler.$description: Scheduler sticky grid headers sit above the scheduler body.

rating.$description: Rating hit targets layer above the star artwork for reliable interaction.

debug.$description: Diagnostic UI is intentionally the highest authored application layer.

breakpoint.$description: Breakpoint debugging remains visible above all application and feature layers.
